sentences.text: Heard on IA No.23173/2023, an application under Section 301(2) of the Cr.P.C.
For the reasons stated in the application, the same is allowed and Shri Devansh Mishra - learned counsel for the complainant and his associate are permitted to assist the prosecution.

The first bail application has been filed by the applicant under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant who is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.484/2023 registered at Police Station- Dehat Basoda, District Vidisha (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 376, 452 and 506-II of the IPC.

sentences.text: per the case of prosecution, prosecutrix reported to PS Dehat Basoda, District Vidisha on 02/12/2023 at 17.58 hours that she is resident of Rajendra Nagar (0.5 km away from PS Dehat Basoda, District Vidisha).
On 30/11/2023 around 2.00 in the afternoon, she was alone at her home.
Her distant relative, accused Ajay Kushwah entered her home and committed rape on her.
Around 3' O clock her husband returned home, she informed her husband and sister-in-law.
As Ajay Kushwah had threatened to kill her, she did not report immediately.
On such allegations, PS Dehat Basoda, District Vidisha registered FIR at Crime No. 484/2023 for the offence punishable under Sections 376, 452 and 506-II of the IPC.
Prosecutrix was forwarded for medico-legal examination.
No definite opinion was given by Medical Officer, as no sign of external or internal injury was found.
Statements of complainant was recorded under Section 161 and 164 of the Cr.P.C.
Statements of other witnesses have also been recorded.
Investigation is underway.
Learned counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that applicant is falsely implicated in this matter.
It is a case of consensual relationship.
Applicant is implicated under the pressure of family.

Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that FIR has been lodged after delay of two days without any plausible explanation which goes to show that applicant is implicated after pre-meditation and pre-consultation.
Applicant is aged 21 years.
There is no likelihood of his absconsion leaving behind his family, home and agricultural field.
No custodial interrogation is required in the matter.
There is no likelihood of tampering with the evidence, as both the parties relate to same socio-economic status.
Jail incarceration on false allegations would bring social disrepute and great hardship to young applicant.
Applicant is ready to cooperate in the investigation.

Therefore, the applicant may be extended the benefit of anticipatory bail Per contra, learned counsel for the State assisted by learned counsel for the objector/complainant opposes the bail application.
Learned counsel submits that family of the applicant is threatening the complainant to withdraw the complaint.
Therefor, applicant may not be extended benefit of anticipatory bail.

On requests of the Court, learned counsel for the State goes through the statement recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C and submits that prosecutrix has stated that while accused was committing rape on her, her husband arrived and rescued her.
Thereafter, accused fled away.
Whereas in her statement recorded under Section 161 of the Cr.P.C, complainant has stated that her husband came after around one hour of the incident.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary and documents.

Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.
Thus, the application is allowed.
